starterFormulas.name: Classic Natural Beeswax Lip Balm
steps: Weigh all ingredients. A 100 g batch fills about 20–22 standard 0.15 oz tubes after normal pouring loss.
Combine beeswax, cocoa butter, shea butter, sweet almond oil, jojoba oil, and castor oil. Melt gently to 75–80 °C until completely clear and uniform.
Hold briefly at temperature, then cool relatively quickly toward 60–65 °C (a cool water bath helps) to reduce shea recrystallization/graininess.
At 60–65 °C, stir in vitamin E T-50 and peppermint essential oil until evenly dispersed.
Pour at 58–62 °C into tubes or tins, slightly overfilling / doming the surface to offset beeswax shrinkage. Top off once if a sinkhole forms.
Leave undisturbed until fully set (several hours at room temperature, or briefly chill after a skin has formed). Cap only when completely cool.
starterFormulas.notes: IFRA Category 1 lip formula with a 1.0% peppermint load at the conservative total-EO comfort cap. Completely anhydrous, so no water-phase preservative is required; vitamin E is an antioxidant only. Deodorized cocoa butter avoids a chocolate note under peppermint. For a nut-free version, replace sweet almond oil 1:1 with a confirmed high-oleic sunflower oil. Verify the peppermint batch IFRA Cat 1 certificate before selling.

starterFormulas.name: Natural Emulsion Body Lotion
steps: Weigh the water phase and the oil phase separately. Heat the distilled water to 70–75 °C; cover to limit evaporation.
In a second vessel, combine Olivem 1000, shea butter, cocoa butter, sweet almond oil, and jojoba oil. Heat to 70–75 °C until the emulsifier and butters are fully melted and clear.
Reweigh the water phase and replenish any evaporated water with freshly heated distilled water before emulsifying, so the formula still totals 100%.
Pour the oil phase into the water phase (or water into oil, consistently) and mix with a stick blender until a uniform, glossy emulsion forms. Continue mixing as it cools.
When the emulsion is below 45 °C, stir in vitamin E T-50, Optiphen Plus, and lavender essential oil until fully dispersed.
Check pH once cooled to room temperature and adjust into 4.8–5.5 if needed (this range is skin-friendly and inside Optiphen Plus’s pH ≤ 6.0 window).
Jar only when cool. Date the batch and store away from heat and sunlight. For anything sold later, run a preservative efficacy (challenge) test.
starterFormulas.notes: O/W lotion using verified in-stock Optiphen Plus at 1.0% (within 0.75–1.5%) because Geogard ECT was not available from the four allowed suppliers on 2026-11-23. If ECT is sourced later, it can replace Optiphen Plus at 1.0% (usage 0.6–1.0%, pH 3–8). Vitamin E is not a preservative. Lavender is 0.5%, inside a conservative IFRA Cat 5A comfort range. Oil phase including emulsifier is 25%, at the Olivem 1000 practical ceiling — do not increase oils without retesting stability.

guardrailRules.message: Ingredient percentages must add up to 100% (tolerance 0.01).
Any formula with water, hydrosol, or another aqueous phase must include a broad-spectrum preservative. Vitamin E and other antioxidants do not count.
Each preservative must be used within its typical usage range (min–max %). Too little may not protect the product; too much can irritate and may be out of spec.
The formula’s target pH must stay inside the preservative’s active pH window. Aim for a skin-friendly 4.5–5.5 when that range also satisfies the preservative.

validation.guidanceMessage: A finished-product pH of 4.5–5.5 is generally more skin-friendly; keep it inside the preservative window as well.

guardrailRules.message: Lip products cannot include any ingredient marked lipSafe: false.

Lip balm essential-oil levels must stay at or below each oil’s maxSafePct.lip and a conservative 1.0% total EO comfort cap. Always verify the supplier’s batch IFRA Category 1 certificate before selling.

For leave-on body lotion, keep total essential oils in a typical 0.5–1.5% range, warn above 2.0%, and block any single oil above its maxSafePct.bodyLotion. Verify the batch IFRA Category 5A certificate before selling.

Phototoxic cold-pressed citrus oils (bergamot, bitter orange, lemon, lime, grapefruit) are flagged in leave-on products. Sweet orange and steam-distilled or FCF (furanocoumarin-free) grades are generally non-phototoxic, but still confirm the grade.

validation.exceptionsNote: Sweet orange (Citrus Aurantium Dulcis / Citrus Sinensis) and steam-distilled or FCF grades are treated as non-phototoxic when phototoxic is false.

guardrailRules.message: Add preservatives, vitamin E, and essential oils in cool-down: below 45 °C for emulsions, and below 65 °C for anhydrous balms.

INCI lists go in descending order by % weight down to 1.0%. Ingredients strictly below 1.0% may be listed in any order after that line. List water as Aqua (or Water (Aqua)). Expand multi-component raw materials to their constituent INCI names and merge duplicates.
